rows.name: PYTHON_VERSION
rows.read_by: Workflow steps that run `uv sync`, and the step that runs `make deb` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`, `.github/workflows/cpp-coverage.yml` and 2 more files)
rows.values: Python version text with major, minor and patch numbers. All 5 workflows set `3.12.7`.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. Each of the 5 workflows that read it defines it at workflow level.
rows.effect: The steps pass it to `uv sync --python` (`uv` is the Python package tool). The CI Python environments then use this Python version. `publish-deb.yml` passes it to `make deb` as `TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION`.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh` reads the workflow text, not the environment. It fails when two workflows give different values, when a value lacks the patch number, or when a value differs from the `TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION` default in `GNUmakefile`.

rows.name: REGIONAL_NIX_CACHE
rows.values: URL of a Nix binary cache. The workflow sets `http://10.202.0.10:5000`. No script checks the text.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. The workflow defines it at workflow level.
rows.effect: Four steps pass it to `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py --cache`. The script copies one Nix store path from this cache with `nix copy --from`. The paths are outputs of the jobs `build-ingest`, `build-model-traces` and `generate-plugins`.
rows.notes: No script reads the name from the environment. `acquire.py` repeats a failed copy until 2700 seconds (45 minutes) have passed.

rows.name: REQUESTED_RUNNER_CLASS
rows.read_by: Steps `Validate refresh invocation` and `Select runner matrix` of job `plan` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
rows.values: `all`, `2x96core` or `2x72core`. Other text stops `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` with `unknown runner class` and exit status 1.
rows.default: Unset: job `plan` always defines it. The value is `all` when the workflow input `runner_class` is empty, as on a scheduled run.
rows.effect: Selects the runner classes (groups of CI servers of one type) that the Slice cost-data refresh measures. `all` selects `2x96core`, and also `2x72core` when `SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED` is `true`.
rows.notes: Unless `SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED` is `true`, the value `2x72core` stops the job with `2x72core refreshes are disabled`. The steps pass the value as a command-line argument. No script reads the name from the environment.

rows.name: ROLLOUT_ENABLED
rows.values: Copy of the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED`. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` compares the text with `true`. Any other text counts as not enabled.
rows.default: Unset: job `plan` always defines it. The value is empty when the repository variable is not defined. Empty counts as not enabled.
rows.effect: Without `true`, `validate-invocation` stops a scheduled run with `scheduled refresh rollout is disabled`. It stops a manual run that is not a dry run with `publishing refresh rollout is disabled`.
rows.notes: The step passes the value as a command-line argument. No script reads the name from the environment. A dry run is a manual run with the workflow input `dry_run` set to `true`.

rows.name: RUN_ATTEMPT
rows.read_by: Step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Whole number from the workflow expression `github.run_attempt`. The step tests whether it is greater than `1`.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. The step always defines it.
rows.effect: A value above `1` adds `--force` to `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh`. The script then runs the benchmark again and does not reuse a stored result of an earlier run.
rows.notes: Only this step reads it. `run_benchmark.sh` does not read the name from the environment.

rows.name: RUN_TESTS
rows.read_by: Step conditions `env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'` in the test jobs (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: `true` or `false`. A workflow expression computes the text. The step conditions compare it with `true`.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. Each job that reads it defines it in its `env` block.
rows.effect: Steps with the condition `env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'` run only when the value is `true`. The value is `false` on a first attempt when a test pass is already recorded for the same source and build.
rows.notes: `cmake-single-platform.yml` computes it from `needs.build.outputs.artifact_verified`. `gcp-nix.yml` computes it from `needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required`. Both give `true` when `github.run_attempt` is above `1`. No script reads the name from the environment.

rows.name: SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X72CORE
rows.who_sets: GitHub repository settings. No file in the repository sets it.
rows.read_by: Job `refresh` of the Slice cost-data refresh, as `EXPECTED_BITFILE` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`, `bin/ci/bench_refresh_matrix.py`, `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py`)
rows.values: Bitfile identity text `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>`, for example `aa.bb.cc.dd@2026-01-02`. The script compares the lower-case text with the identity of the FPGA cards. It does not check the format.

rows.effect: The refresh job for runner class `2x72core` gets the value as `EXPECTED_BITFILE`. When the FPGA cards report another bitfile identity, the measurement stops with `bitfile mismatch`.
rows.notes: The name is not in the workflow file. The matrix field `expected_bitfile_var` from `bin/ci/bench_refresh_matrix.py` selects it. A value in another format never matches.

rows.who_sets: GitHub repository settings. No file in the repository sets it.
rows.read_by: Job `refresh` of the Slice cost-data refresh, as `EXPECTED_BITFILE` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`, `bin/ci/bench_refresh_matrix.py`, `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py`)
rows.values: Bitfile identity text `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>`, for example `aa.bb.cc.dd@2026-01-02`. The script compares the lower-case text with the identity of the FPGA cards. It does not check the format.
rows.default: Unset: no identity is required. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` still requires one identity on all FPGA cards and the complete device list.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED
rows.who_sets: GitHub repository settings. No file in the repository sets it.
rows.read_by: Job `plan` of the Slice cost-data refresh and job `health` of its health check (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`, `.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`, `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`)
rows.values: Only the exact text `true` enables. Any other text counts as not enabled.
rows.default: Unset: only runner class `2x96core` is refreshed. The health check expects only `2x96core`.
rows.effect: `true` adds runner class `2x72core` to the Slice cost-data refresh. The health check (the workflow that looks for recent refresh runs) then also expects `2x72core`.
rows.notes: Job `plan` copies it to `ENABLE_2X72`. Without `true`, the value `all` of the workflow input `runner_class` selects only `2x96core`. The value `2x72core` stops job `plan` with `2x72core refreshes are disabled`.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_ALERT_ASSIGNEES
rows.who_sets: GitHub repository settings. `.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml` copies it into the environment of job `reconcile`.
rows.values: GitHub user names in the form that `gh issue edit --add-assignee` accepts. The script passes the text unchanged and does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: a new health issue gets no assignee.
rows.effect: When `reconcile-health` creates the issue `Slice cost-data refresh is unhealthy`, it assigns the issue to these users. An open issue with that title only gets a comment.
rows.notes: When the `gh issue edit` call fails, the script prints a `::warning::` line and continues. `bin/slice-tests/test_bench_refresh_workflow.py` sets `missing-user` to test that case.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_BITFILE
rows.who_sets: No file in the repository sets it. A person who runs `bin/ci/bench_refresh.py` by hand can set it.
rows.values: Any text. The script does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the `bitfile` row shows `<not provided>`. Empty: the row shows empty text.
rows.effect: Sets the `bitfile` row of the Markdown summary that the script writes to the `--summary` file. The script reads it only when the option `--bitfile-metadata` is absent.
rows.notes: The Slice cost-data refresh does not use it. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` always passes `--bitfile-metadata`. The row then shows the bitfile identity and the device count from that JSON file.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
rows.values: Whole number of seconds from `60` to `5400`, written with 2 to 5 digits. Other non-empty text stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.default: Unset: the measurement limit is 5400 seconds (90 minutes).
rows.effect: Replaces the limit of 5400 seconds that `run-measurement` gives to the `bin/slice submit` measurement command through `timeout`.
rows.notes: The workflow sets it from the input `measurement_timeout_seconds`. Job `plan` accepts that input only for a manual dry run. On a scheduled run, `SLICE_REFRESH_STOP_UTC` can shorten the limit further.

evidence.quote: echo "measurement timeout override must be between 60 and 5400 seconds" \

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_REVIEWERS
rows.who_sets: GitHub repository settings. `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml` copies it into the environment of job `publish`.
rows.values: Reviewer names in the form that `gh pr edit --add-reviewer` accepts. The script passes the text unchanged and does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the refresh pull request gets no review request.
rows.effect: After `upsert-pr` creates or updates the refresh pull request, it requests a review from these reviewers.
rows.notes: The refresh pull request updates `config/test-benchmarks.json`. When the `gh pr edit` call fails, the script prints a `::warning::` line and continues.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED
rows.who_sets: GitHub repository settings. No file in the repository sets it.
rows.read_by: Job conditions of the Slice cost-data refresh and of its health check (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`, `.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`, `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`)
rows.values: Only the exact text `true` enables. Any other text counts as not enabled.
rows.default: Unset: scheduled runs of the refresh and of the health check skip all jobs. A manual refresh run works only as a dry run.
rows.effect: `true` turns on the scheduled Slice cost-data refresh, the publication of its pull request and the scheduled health check. It also permits a manual refresh run that is not a dry run.
rows.notes: Job `plan` copies it to `ROLLOUT_ENABLED`. Publication also requires a run on the default branch. A manual health check does not need the variable.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_RUNNER_CLASS
rows.who_sets: No file in the repository sets it. A person who runs `bin/ci/bench_refresh.py` by hand can set it.
rows.values: Any text. The script does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the `runner class` row shows `<not provided>`. Empty: the row shows empty text.
rows.effect: Sets the `runner class` row of the Markdown summary that the script writes to the `--summary` file. It is the default of the option `--runner-class`.
rows.notes: The option `--runner-class` wins over the variable. The Slice cost-data refresh does not use the variable. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` always passes `--runner-class`.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_RUN_URL
rows.who_sets: No file in the repository sets it. A person who runs `bin/ci/bench_refresh.py` by hand can set it.
rows.values: Any non-empty text. The script does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the script builds the run URL from `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and `GITHUB_RUN_ID`. When one of them is empty, the text is `<not provided>`.
rows.effect: Sets the `workflow run` row of the Markdown summary that the script writes to the `--summary` file. It is the default of the option `--run-url`.
rows.notes: The option `--run-url` wins over the variable. The Slice cost-data refresh does not use the variable. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` always passes `--run-url`.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_SOURCE_SHA
rows.who_sets: No file in the repository sets it. A person who runs `bin/ci/bench_refresh.py` by hand can set it.
rows.values: Any text. The script does not parse it. With `--expected-names`, the text must equal the `source_sha` field of that file.
rows.default: Unset: the value of `GITHUB_SHA`, or `<not provided>` when that is unset too. Empty: the script uses the empty text and ignores `GITHUB_SHA`.
rows.effect: Sets the `source SHA` row of the Markdown summary. The script also writes the text into the `--write-expected-names` file. It is the default of the option `--source-sha`.
rows.notes: The option `--source-sha` wins over the variable. A mismatch with the `--expected-names` file stops the script with `expected names source mismatch`. The Slice cost-data refresh does not use the variable. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` always passes `--source-sha`.

rows.name: SLICE_REFRESH_STOP_UTC
rows.values: Time of day in UTC, written `HH:MM:SS`. The workflow sets `06:30:00`. The script passes the text to `date -u -d` and does not check it.
rows.default: Unset: `06:30:00` UTC.
rows.effect: On a scheduled run, the measurement limit is at most the time until this time of the current UTC day, minus 30 seconds. A limit below 60 seconds stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.notes: The script reads it only when `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` is `schedule`. The 30 seconds are the kill grace period that the `timeout` command gets as `--kill-after`.

rows.name: SOURCE_HASH
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py`, and steps of the jobs `test` and `benchmark` (`bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Exactly 7 lower-case hexadecimal characters. Other text stops `prepare_handoff.py` with `invalid seven-hex source hash` and exit status 2.
rows.default: Unset: `prepare_handoff.py` requires the option `--source-hash`. Empty: the script stops with `invalid seven-hex source hash`.
rows.effect: Identifies the tracked source files. `prepare_handoff.py` uses it as the directory name of the test pass marker (an empty file that records passed tests). The script also copies it to the output `source_hash`.
rows.notes: The step `Identify source` of job `tron-build` computes it from `git ls-files -s` and writes it to the `GITHUB_ENV` file. The jobs `test` and `benchmark` pass it on the command line. The option `--source-hash` wins over the variable.

rows.name: SOURCE_SHA
rows.values: Full git commit id: exactly 40 lower-case hexadecimal characters. The script checks the text only when the option `--receipt` is given.
rows.default: Unset: no value. With `--receipt`, the script stops with `runtime receipt requires a full source commit SHA` and exit status 2.
rows.effect: `prepare_handoff.py` writes it as `source_sha` into the JSON receipt file that the option `--receipt` names.
rows.notes: The step `Identify source` of job `tron-build` writes the output of `git rev-parse HEAD` to the `GITHUB_ENV` file. The option `--source-sha` wins over the variable. Without `--receipt` the script does not use the value.

evidence.quote: if source_sha is None or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", source_sha):

rows.name: TEST_ENVIRONMENT_STORE_PATH
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py`, `bin/ci/nix-cache/publish_lab.py` and workflow steps (`bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py`, `bin/ci/nix-cache/publish_lab.py`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` and 1 more file)
rows.values: Path that resolves through symbolic links to one Nix store root: `/nix/store/`, 32 characters, `-`, a name. Both scripts reject other paths.
rows.default: Unset: `prepare_handoff.py` requires the option `--test-environment`. `publish_lab.py` stops with a `KeyError`. Empty: both scripts reject the path.
rows.effect: Names the Nix test environment (the Nix store path with the tools of the CI test jobs). `prepare_handoff.py` writes the resolved path to its outputs. `publish_lab.py` queues it for publication to the lab Nix cache.
rows.notes: In `prepare_handoff.py` the option `--test-environment` wins over the variable. In the test jobs and in the refresh job, a step sets it and passes it to `test_runtime.py --environment-store-path` on the command line.

new_terms.definition: The workflow `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`. It runs a full `bin/slice bench` measurement on each selected runner class. It then opens a pull request that updates `config/test-benchmarks.json`.
A group of self-hosted CI servers of one type. The Slice cost-data refresh knows `2x96core` and `2x72core`.

new_terms.term: health check (of the Slice cost-data refresh)
new_terms.definition: The workflow `.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`. It fails when an expected runner class has no measured and published refresh in the last 14 days. It then opens or updates the issue `Slice cost-data refresh is unhealthy`.

new_terms.term: dry run (of the Slice cost-data refresh)
new_terms.definition: A manual run of the refresh workflow with the input `dry_run` set to `true`. It measures and applies the result, and it opens no pull request.
The text `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>` that `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` builds from the release code and the release date that each FPGA card reports.
An empty file `<root>/<source hash>/nix-tests-<identity>.passed`. It records that the tests passed for one source hash, one test build and one Nix test environment.
The Nix store path with the tools that the CI test jobs run, for example `python3` and `uv`.
A top-level path of the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`. A path inside such a directory is not a store root.
The Nix binary cache at the URL in `LAB_NIX_CACHE`. The test jobs and the benchmark jobs on FPGA servers copy their runtimes from it.
The Python package tool that creates the Python environments outside the Nix dev shell.

notes: All 21 variables stay as rows. None is dropped. Source choices: a job-level env entry counts as workflow env (REQUESTED_RUNNER_CLASS, ROLLOUT_ENABLED, RUN_TESTS, SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). SOURCE_HASH and SOURCE_SHA count as step env: a step of job tron-build writes them to the GITHUB_ENV file, and later steps of that job see them. The four names that only bin/ci/bench_refresh.py reads (SLICE_REFRESH_BITFILE, SLICE_REFRESH_RUNNER_CLASS, SLICE_REFRESH_RUN_URL, SLICE_REFRESH_SOURCE_SHA) have source script: no file in the checkout sets them, and bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh always passes the matching options. SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X72CORE and SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X96CORE never become process environment variables under their own names. The workflow reads them as vars[matrix.expected_bitfile_var] and exports the value as EXPECTED_BITFILE. Evidence quotes avoid source lines that hold a pipe character. For that reason the defining expression lines are not quoted for RUN_TESTS (.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml:558 and :625, .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:387), for REQUESTED_RUNNER_CLASS (.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml:61, bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh:54) and for the range test of SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh:28). The example value aa.bb.cc.dd@2026-01-02 for the bitfile identity is made up to show the format that bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py:47 builds. It is not a real bitfile. Default cells of variables that a workflow always defines say so in place of a behaviour for the unset case: the checkout does not show what the step does without the variable. Empty TEST_ENVIRONMENT_STORE_PATH: read from the code, not run. argparse turns the empty default into Path('.'), which resolves to the working directory and fails the store path pattern. The existing documents (README.ci.md, bin/ci/README.md, doc/slice-benchmark-lifecycle.md, README.dependencies.md) agree with the rows for the variables that they mention.
